articles.title: St. Louis Cardinals Promote From Within For New General Manager
articles.summary: The St. Louis Cardinals have promoted 34-year-old Rob Cerfolio to general manager.
articles.body: The St. Louis Cardinals have promoted 34-year-old Rob Cerfolio to general manager. The Cardinals announced the move Friday. Cerfolio has been St. Louis' assistant GM overseeing player development and performance the past three seasons. He'll report to president of baseball operations Chaim Bloom. "Since joining the Cardinals two years ago, Cerf has spearheaded tremendous progress in our player development efforts from top to bottom, and in the advancement of our performance group and its integration within our entire organization," Bloom said. "He is relentless in his desire to move us forward, and is invested in relationships with both new hires and longtime staff alike." Cerfolio’s promotion comes after executive Randy Flores left the team Monday. Flores spent 11 years in St. Louis, including the past eight as assistant GM overseeing amateur and pro acquisitions. Cerfolio joined the Cardinals after spending 10 years working his way up the ranks with the Cleveland Guardians, including his final three seasons as the team’s director of player development. From Indian Springs, Alabama, he's staying in St. Louis after reportedly being a candidate to fill several front-office openings this offseason. The Cardinals are coming off a 77-85 season in which they finished fourth in the National League Central and missed the playoffs for a fourth consecutive season. Cerfolio is a Yale graduate and credited for playing a role in the Cardinals' burgeoning youth movement, highlighted by standout seasons from outfielder Jordan Walker and second baseman JJ Wetherholt. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Breece Hall Returns After 5-Game Absence, But Jets Rule Out Garrett Wilson
articles.summary: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson remains in concussion protocol and will miss Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson remains in the concussion protocol and was ruled out Friday for the game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday. It's a tough blow for an offense that will get running back Breece Hall back in the lineup after he missed five games with a quadriceps injury. Coach Aaron Glenn said Wilson would not practice for a third straight day after he was injured late in the Jets' 38-33 loss to Las Vegas last Sunday. Wilson has a team-leading 43 catches, tied for the most in the AFC and ninth in the NFL, for 527 yards and three touchdowns. His 63 targets are second in the AFC, though he was frustrated the last few weeks by his sporadic usage in games and in crucial moments. Against the Raiders, Wilson had six receptions for 83 yards on a team-high 12 targets. In the closing moments last Sunday, Wilson took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Jeremy Chinn on a 15-yard catch in which Chinn was called for unnecessary roughness. Wilson stayed in and was Geno Smith’s intended target in the end zone on the next play when Chinn came up with a game-sealing interception. "I mean, I think it speaks for itself," Glenn said of losing Wilson. "Any time you lose a player of that magnitude, it's always tough. But we do have other players and those guys will look forward to the challenge." Adonai Mitchell had a breakout performance last week against Las Vegas, catching seven passes for a career-high 142 yards and a touchdown in his second game back after missing four with a finger injury that required surgery. Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. was held without a target last week, but previously had consecutive 100-yard receiving games. Isaiah Williams, Tim Patrick and rookie Malik McClain are also on the active roster. Sterling Shepard, Jamaal Pritchett and Joseph Manjack IV are on the practice squad. Hall will further boost a backfield that has been solid the last few weeks in his absence. Braelon Allen has rushed for more than 100 yards three times, including a career-high 147 last week. Hall had just 163 yards rushing on 51 carries in three games — which would be a career-low 3.2 yards per attempt — before being hurt at Detroit on Sept. 27. He also had 10 catches for 102 yards. With Allen's emergence, there has been speculation over how the Jets will use the two running backs, but both Glenn and offensive coordinator Frank Reich have insisted since before the season that they envisioned mixing both in the offense as a 1-2 punch out of the backfield. The GOAT Assesses The Favorites "I know we’re trying to get in this, who’s going to be the starter and try to spin it into a negative situation," Glenn said. "But nothing’s changed from how I see this. Both of those guys are playing, that’s just what it is." Rookie edge rusher David Bailey will be back after missing one game with a groin injury. The No. 2 overall pick in the draft in April leads the team with 5.5 sacks. Tight end Mason Taylor, who injured his back late against Las Vegas, will be a full practice participant Friday and is cleared to play. Cornerback Nahshon Wright (back) was sitting out practice Friday and is questionable. Edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) and defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle) are also questionable. Linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) is out. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.body: For the first time in a long time, we won't be seeing Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo patrolling the pitch for their respective countries. With both icons now retired from international duty, we close out the calendar year that saw Spain lift the 2026 World Cup with a final November window that will feature some top-bill matches, especially in Europe. Several heavyweight squads — Spain, England, and Portugal – dropped their rosters for the final matches of the UEFA Nations League group stage. That includes a contest between Spain and England on Nov. 15 in Madrid that will now carry some emotional weight. Here are my takeaways from some of the more notable roster decisions: 1.Spain Aims To Heal Country After Tragedies Two recent tragedies in Spain – one off the pitch and one on it – reminded us that there are things in life much bigger than football. Against that backdrop, the defending World Cup champions will use the upcoming matches against Czechia and England to help their nation heal. Last Wednesday, a train collision in Urda killed 69 people (and injured 200) on a Madrid-Sevilla high-speed line, making it one of the worst transportation tragedies in European history and the second one in Spain this year. Days later, Jesús de Miguel Alameda, the 30-year-old striker from CD Tenerife, the second-division club from the Canary Islands, died after a collision with Andorra's goalkeeper Jesús Owono in the middle of a match. As Spain’s squad was announced on Friday, manager Luis De La Fuente and the country's federation honored the victims of both tragedies. "Football must unite us today more than ever. We share the grief of the families of the victims from Urda, and we mourn the irreparable loss of Jesús de Miguel," he said before announcing his 27-man list. Jesús de Miguel's funeral was held on Thursday at his family’s village as the insurmountable pain was felt across the country, with Spanish and European clubs paying tributes to him throughout the week. De la Fuente, who has created a family-based environment on and off the pitch for Spain, was present at the funeral alongside Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez. "We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever," said de la Fuente on the day of mourning. It was a touching moment as Spain will undoubtedly use this international window to unite the country during a period of mourning, especially in the second match against England, held at Atlético de articles.title: Sean McVay Gives Myles Garrett Update For Rams; Superstar Poised To Return?
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are expected to activate superstar pass rusher Myles Garrett from injured reserve for Week 9.
articles.body: He's back! Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay expressed in a press conference on Friday afternoon that the team expects to activate superstar linebacker Myles Garrett from injured reserve for their Week 9 road tilt against the Washington Commanders (Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX) "barring any sort of setbacks." Garrett suffered a knee injury in Week 1 that required arthroscopic surgery and landed him on injured reserve. In Garrett's absence, the Rams went 4-3 and are 4-4 altogether this season. Still, as a whole, the Rams' defense is fourth in the NFL in opponent passing yards (191.9 per game), fifth in opponent total yards (301.1 per game), 12th in opponent points (21.0 per game) and 14th in opponent rushing yards (109.3 per game). Of course, they're tied for 26th in the sport with 12.0 sacks, which is an area where Garrett's return will help, among other respects. Last season, Garrett, a five-time All-Pro and seven-time Pro Bowler, set the NFL single-season record with 23 sacks while totaling three forced fumbles, a league-high 33 tackles for loss and 60 combined tackles for the Cleveland Browns. Garrett, a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year (2023 and 2025), averaged 13.9 sacks and 2.6 forced fumbles per season across his nine years with the Browns (2017-25), while also leading the sport in tackles for loss in each of his last two seasons in Cleveland (2024-25). The Rams acquired Garrett from the Browns in June for defensive end and 2024 first-round pick Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-rounder and a 2029 third-rounder. Elsewhere for the Rams, cornerback Jaylen Watson has been placed on season-ending injured reserve due to a shoulder injury that requires surgery.

articles.title: Brady Returns: The Top 5 Tom Brady-Rob Gronkowski Plays At Gillette Stadium
articles.summary: As Tom Brady and Rob Gronkowski return to their old stomping grounds, here are their five best plays at Gillette Stadium.
articles.body: Sunday's Green Bay Packers-New England Patriots game will not only serve as a homecoming for one GOAT, but it will also be a special day for another. As Tom Brady is set to call his first game at Gillette Stadium, Rob Gronkowski will be inducted into the Patriots Hall of Fame over the weekend. Gronkowski arguably became the greatest tight end in NFL history during his nine seasons in New England, winning three Super Bowls, being named a Pro Bowler five times and setting numerous records at the position. With Gronkowski setting a new standard for excellence at tight end and becoming one of the key figures of the Patriots' dynasty run, it's easy to wonder if he'll also get a statue outside of Gillette Stadium someday, just like Brady. In fact, Brady was asked if Gronkowski will get a statue outside of Gillette Stadium sometime down the road in the latest edition of "#AskTom." Brady not only said yes, but he also gave Patriots fans an idea on how they could build a statue for him this weekend. "I actually think we need to crowdsource beer cans this weekend and the fans will build the statue themselves," Brady said. "I'll come out, I'll get it in on the action and that would be a true testament to the Gronk mentality. It would warm my heart." Brady connecting on a beer can toss to Gronk to help build a statue would be the latest of several memorable connections they've had over the years. The 105 touchdowns (including playoffs) that Brady threw to Gronkowski are the second-most by any quarterback-receiver duo in NFL history. But as Brady and Gronkowski return to their old stomping ground this week, which five plays between the two of them were the best at Gillette Stadium? Here are the top five Brady-to-Gronkowski plays at Gillette Stadium. 5.Gronk Hauls In Brady's Perfect Arc Pass For TD vs. Steelers (2015) When you've thrown 105 touchdown passes to one player, you can certainly trust that receiver to come down with a 50/50 ball. That's what Brady did with Gronkowski on numerous occasions in his career. One notable instance came in Week 1 of the 2015 season. Lining up in a goal-line formation, Brady ran a play-action fake and threw a lob to Gronkowski in the back of the end zone. Gronkowski used his size to perfectly get himself in position to grab the ball, while somehow keeping his feet inbounds to successfully come down with the touchdown grab. Gronkowski absolutely dominated the Pittsburgh Steelers in that game as well. He caught five passes for 94 yards — and three of those catches were touchdown grabs. That was practically an average showing for Gronkowski against the Steelers in his career. He had 41 catches for 685 yards and eight touchdowns in seven career games against Pittsburgh. 4.Gronk Catches Back Shoulder Fade With One Hand vs. Bills (2017) Another instance where Brady trusted Gronkowski to come down with a 50/50 ball, but this reception was a bit more difficult. Gronkowski was lined out wide and ran a fade along the sideline toward the end zone, with Buffalo Bills safety Micah Hyde running in lockstep with him. However, Brady was able to place the ball in a place where Gronkowski could only get it. Gronkowski made a back shoulder grab, only needing one hand to haul in the reception for a 17-yard touchdown. That catch helped spark a 37-16 win for the Patriots, with Gronkowski recording five receptions for 67 yards and a touchdown in that game. 3.Gronk Turns Routine Catch Into TD Thanks To Stiff Arm vs. Bears (2014) While there were many instances when Brady trusted Gronkowski to come down with a 50/50 grab, this play against the Chicago Bears was one where the all-time great tight end made the magic happen himself. Brady threw a low strike to Gronkowski over the middle, getting it by a diving Bears defender. After Gronkowski caught the ball at his ankles, he threw a stiff arm to get one would-be tackler off of him before dragging another would-be tackler five yards and into the end zone for a 47-yard touchdown. Gronkowski had nine receptions for 149 yards and three touchdowns in a whopping 51-23 win for the Patriots that day. 2.Gronk Makes Diving TD Grab vs. Broncos In Divisional Round (2011) Gronkowski brought a highlight to remember in one of his first playoff games. With the Patriots looking to tack onto their early 7-0 lead, Brady found Gronkowski in the back corner of the end zone, but it wasn't an easy catch for the tight end. Gronkowski needed to make a diving effort as he juggled the ball while falling to the turf. Gronkowski was able to reel in the grab and did his classic Gronk Spike afterward as the Patriots took a 14-0 lead. That was the first of three touchdown grabs for Gronkowski in that game, as he logged 10 catches for 145 yards in a 45-10 win for the Patriots in the divisional round matchup. 1.Gronk Reels In Impossible One-Handed Grab vs. Broncos (2014) Somehow, Gronkowski's catch against the Broncos in 2011 wasn't the best catch he made against Denver in his career. A few seasons later, Gronkowski showed why he was one of the most dominant players in the history of the sport with his one-handed grab against the Broncos in 2014. As Brady pump-faked and struggled to find an open receiver, he eventually said screw it and decided to throw a pass to Gronkowski, even though he had a few Broncos defenders around him. The throw from Brady wasn't perfect, as the ball went to Gronkowski's left as he was running right. He also had Broncos safety T.J. Ward draped all over him. Still, Gronkowski came down with a 20-yard reception as he grabbed the pass with his left hand. He caught a touchdown pass on the next play as part of a nine-catch, 105-yard day in a 43-21 win over the Broncos, which also featured a memorable image of Denver triple covering Gronkowski. articles.title: Khushbu's Youth Olympics silver gives Siddi community a new sporting hero
articles.summary: PANAJI: Now based in London, former India goalkeeper Juje Siddi has not been following all that’s happening in Indian sports, but Khushbu Darjada’s silver
articles.body: PANAJI: Now based in London, former India goalkeeper Juje Siddi has not been following all that’s happening in Indian sports, but Khushbu Darjada’s silver medal at the Youth Olympics didn’t escape his attention.Darjada took silver in the women’s judo 63kg category in Senegal, the first Olympic medal won by any member of the Siddi community.“This is good news for everyone, particularly the community,” said Juje, the first from the Siddi tribe to represent the country and win gold at the SAFF Championship in 1997. “The feat will motivate so many others from the community to take to sport and win laurels.”Ever since his move to Salgaocar SC in 1994, Juje has stood out for his distinctive look and ‘African’ features. The goalkeeper belongs to the marginalised Siddi community, descendants of East Africans who were brought to India more than five centuries ago. The Siddis have lived in relative seclusion, most on the margins of poverty.“In the 90s, we had good support (from the govt) but now that’s no longer the case. There is private coaching being conducted but coaches are not serious enough. You must prioritise the interest of the community. If the govt steps in, there’s plenty to gain. Siddis are genetically built strong, have great physique and very good in sports,” said the Karwar-born Juje.In 1987, the Sports Authority of India (SAI), spearheaded by the then Union minister of sports Margaret Alva, set up a sports scheme to scout and train members of the community. The Siddi people had athletic abilities, and Juje was among those scouted as part of the Special Area Games (SAG) scheme.He was scouted as an athlete, but when he moved to Bengaluru for schooling, his goalkeeping abilities got noticed. He did well and made it to the India U-16 camp. His selection to the India U-19 team convinced him that he was on the right track.Soon, he was spotted by coach Norbert Gonsalves during a camp in Patiala for Salgaocar.“We were lucky to be part of the SAG scheme. They suddenly stopped the project,” said the goalkeeper.The goalkeeper enjoyed a memorable career with Salgaocar, winning every major trophy in Indian football, including the National Football League in 1999.After his retirement, he took to coaching. Juje had to move to the UK in 2019. Now, at 53, he wants to return and give back to the community that shaped him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Azzi Fudd's breakup with Paige Bueckers sparks fresh questions about her WNBA future and Dallas Wings connection
articles.summary: Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers are no longer together, and they say the split happened more than a year ago.
articles.body: Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers are no longer together, and they say the split happened more than a year ago. The Dallas Wings teammates shared it on November 6 during an episode of Fudd’s podcast, “Fudd Around and Find Out.” The timing is the real news. They broke up before Dallas took Fudd first overall in April, and before they shared a locker room for the 2026 season. Bueckers also dismissed any idea that their relationship shaped the pick. Neither player shared details about why it ended, and Fudd made clear the rest stays private.Azzi Fudd and Paige Bueckers confirm breakup on podcastBoth laughed at the start, but Fudd kept it blunt. “We are no longer together. I don’t know how else to say that,” she said. Bueckers gave the timeline. “It’s been over a year.”Then she took on the draft chatter. “We were not together before she got drafted, so all of those narratives can go to bed,” Bueckers said. “She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it.” That second line matters because Dallas never answered the question when it first came up. At Fudd’s introductory press conference in April, a reporter asked if the two were still a couple. Wings public relations cut in before Fudd could speak.The online noise pushed them to speak. “We’ve seen a lot of negativity. We’ve seen a lot of hate,” Bueckers said, and she added that messages had reached their families and friends. Her explanation for the split was short. “Sometimes in life, there’s just seasons.”What the breakup means for Fudd and the WingsThe split did not hurt the basketball. Fudd averaged 13.1 points as a rookie, fourth among first-year players, and shot 39.7 percent from three. That shooting gives Bueckers more room to work. Bueckers made her second straight All-Star team.Dallas won a franchise-record 27 games and made the playoffs for the first time in three years. The Wings then lost in the first round to Golden State, which went on to win the title. Because the breakup came before the season, the team played every game with two former No. 1 picks who were no longer a couple. That makes this a fair test, and the results held up. It also makes them the first college teammates to go first overall in back-to-back drafts since Tina Charles in 2010 and Maya Moore in 2011.Bueckers said both will eventually move on and see other people. Until then, the work comes first. “We’re the utmost professional. We care about basketball, and we’re still friends,” she said. Fudd had a request for fans too: “we don’t need messages on what the other person is doing.”For Dallas, 2027 comes down to basketball. Can Fudd keep shooting near 40 percent in year two? articles.title: Collin Dixon's 2 TD catches help Illinois become bowl eligible with 24-13 victory over Nebraska
articles.summary: (AP) — Collin Dixon caught two touchdown passes including a record-breaker and Illinois used a trick play to set up its go-ahead TD as the Illini defeated Ne...
articles.body:
CHAMPAIGN, Ill. (AP) — Collin Dixon caught two touchdown passes including a record-breaker and Illinois used a trick play to set up its go-ahead TD as the Illini defeated Nebraska 24-13 on Friday night to become bowl eligible with their fourth straight victory.

Dixon's 3- and 6-yard TD receptions gave him 12 for the year, breaking Illinois' all-time single-season mark by two. He caught eight passes for 129 yards from Katin Houser, who was 22 of 36 through the air for 292 yards and three TDs.

A 29-yard run by holder Lars Rau on a fake field goal set up the go-ahead TD for Illinois (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten Conference) early in the third quarter — a 5-yard pass from Houser to Jordan Anderson.

Rau, who is the Illini's punter, said the fake is called "Charlie Brown."

"It worked because everyone did their part," he said.

Nebraska coach Matt Ruhle said his team was prepared for the fake, but the Illini still pulled it off.

"They called something aggressive, executed it, and made the play," he said.

Illinois coach Bret Bielema said while he's happy his team is bowl eligible, "a 9-3 team can get into the playoffs."

Nebraska (5-4, 2-4) lost its fourth straight. Anthony Colandrea was 32 of 43 for 284 yards and a TD to Jacory Brown Jr., who had six catches for 93 yards. Jamal Rule ran for 69 yards on 15 carries.

"I know everyone is frustrated, but when you look at the game, it was a good one for a long time," Ruhle said. "We just needed to make a couple more plays."

Dixon scrambled into the end zone on a 3-yard TD pass from Houser late in the first half on his record-breaking reception to tie the game 7-7 at halftime.

Nebraska took a 7-0 lead early in the second quarter on a 15-yard run by Mekhi Nelson on his only carry of the game. The Huskers drove 98 yards in 10 plays for the score.

Nebraska kicker John Hohl missed 54- and 45-yard field goals in the half.

Nebraska: The Huskers got off to a 5-0 start this season for the first time since 2016, then suffered three straight heartbreaking losses by a total of 13 points. They led each of those games in the fourth quarter, irritating their rabid fanbase. Nebraska's loss Friday night won't help matters in Lincoln.

Illinois: Early-season home losses to Duke and Purdue seemingly put a damper on the Illini's bowl chances. But Illinois has bounced back with four straight wins, much needed victories heading into a tough stretch to end the regular season (at No. 5 UCLA, home vs. No. 21 Iowa and at Northwestern). Only UCLA (5-0) has a longer Big Ten winning streak than Illinois, which is eligible for a third straight bowl appearance for the first time since 1992.

Nebraska has held teams to less than 100 yards rushing six times, with a season-low 32 yards vs. Washington. Illinois had only 84 yards on the ground.

Dixon's school record TD catch came on the drive after Illini running back Javari Barnett was carted off the field with his injured left leg in an air cast.

articles.title: Michael Salgado-Medina’s FG caps late Arizona comeback to beat TCU
articles.summary: Who said nothing good happens after midnight? Down eight points with less than two minutes to go, Arizona pulled out some late magic to rally for a 29-28 win...
articles.body:
Who said nothing good happens after midnight?

Down eight points with less than two minutes to go, Arizona pulled out some late magic to rally for a 29-28 win over TCU on Friday night at Casino Del Sol Stadium.

Michael Salgado-Medina kicked a 37-yard field goal with 38 seconds to go, his third FG of the game and a score that came after the Wildcats (7-2, 4-2 Big 12) recovered an onside kick. The UA had to try the trick play after scoring a touchdown with 1:45 left but missing the 2-point conversion.

The winning kick came at 12:05 a.m. Tucson time, then two minutes later Tyrese Boss iced it with an interception.

It was the 7 th straight win for Arizona at home, the longest streak since eight in a row in 1993-94.

TCU (4-5, 2-4) took a 28-20 lead with 6:35 left on a 2-yard run by quarterback Jaden Craig , who threw for 232 yards and a TD on 28-of-40 passing with two rushing scores. Despite being down eight, Arizona didn't rush and moved into the red zone with under three minutes left on a 16-yard catch by Isaiah Mizell .

Mizell had six catches for 78 yards and a TD while teammate Giovanni Richardson had 11 catches for 171 yards.

Arizona's comeback was almost thrwarted on the next play when Quincy Craig fumbled but Noah Fifita fell on the loose ball at the 15. Two plays later, Fifita and Craig connected on a 15-yard TD pass with 1:45 left.

It was the second TD pass of the game for Fifita, who was 24 of 37 for 313 yards with an interception as well as a rushing score, the 6 th time in his career he's run for a TD and thrown for at least one.

Fifita's 2-point pass was incomplete, keeping the UA down 2. Despite having three timeouts it opted for an onside kick, but rather than the standard ground skinner Ian French pooched it deep.

TCU's Ed Small muffed the ball as he ran back to try and catch it, and seldom-used defensive back Zuri Watson recovered at the Frogs' 26. After three runs to get the Frogs to use their timeouts, Salgado-Medina drilled the 37-yarder.

Boss then picked off Craig on the first play after the ensuing kickoff, one of the few solid plays by a secondary that was missing two starters and saw another get hurt during the game. The Wildcats were flagged five times for pass interference, three on Dwight Bootle II and two on Boss.

TCU led 14-10 at halftime and got the ball first, getting into Arizona territory before stalling and settling for a 50-yard field goal. Tre Smith busted through the line and blocked it, his second blocked kick of the season.

Arizona capitalized, with Fifita scoring on a 9-yard run to go back up 17-14 with 8:14 left in the 3 rd . The play before saw Fifita scramble to his left and find Richardson behind the defense for a 36-yard catch.

TCU went 75 yards in 11 plays, converting a pair of third downs along the way, to retake the lead at 21-17 on a 7-yard catch by Jordan Dwyer with 2:39 left in the third. Bootle was victimized multiple times on the drive, including picking up his second pass interference penalty.

Arizona quickly got in position to go in front again after a 46-yard catch by Richardson down to the TCU 9. But the Frogs' defense held and Salgado – Medina hit a 23-yard field goal on the first play of the 4 th quarter, cutting the deficit to 21-20.

The UA defense did its part right after that, forcing a quick punt with Tre Smith sacking Craig on 3 rd and long. But the Wildcats went 3-and-out, getting stopped on a 3 rd and short run.

TCU converted a pair of 3 rd and longs on the ensuing drive, then a third pass interference call on Bootle set up a 2-yard TD run by Craig. The Frogs opted for the PAT to make it an 8-point game with 6:35 to go.

Arizona had one of its best opening drives of the season, going 75 yards in 10 plays capped by Mizell's diving catch for a 20-yard TD.

After TCU went 3-and-out on its first possession, that included a Cooper Blomstrom sack, Arizona got three via a 43-yard Salgado-Medina field goal. The drive was kept alive by an offsides call on the Horned Frogs on a 3 rd down play that had resulted in a sack.

The Horned Frogs had their first scoring opportunity early in the 2 nd quarter, getting down to the UA 15. They lined up to go for it on 4 th and inches, called a timeout and then afterwards were called for a false start and instead opted for a 37-yard field goal that was wide right.

A pair of Arizona penalties helped get TCU on the board a few minutes later. First, a hold on Tristan Bounds negated a nice run gain, instead resulting in a 3-and-out, then the a pass interference againstBootle gave the Frogs 1 st and goal which led toCraig scoring on a 7-yard run to make it 10-7 with 8:53 left in the 2 nd .

The run keyed a trip into the red zone on Arizona's next possession, getting inside the 10, but on 3 rd down Fifita tried to hitRichardson but TCU linebacker Hudson Hooper dropped into coverage and picked it off for a 93-yard interception return TD and a 14-10 lead with 4:09 to go before halftime.

Arizona is back home next week to take on No. 3 Utah. The Utes (8-0, 5-0) host No. 7 BYU on Saturday.

articles.title: Merritt Island Christian wins thriller, advances to state semifinals
articles.summary: In a back-and-forth game, Merritt Island Christian made the final stand in a 51-50 win over Bradenton Christian to advance to the state semifinals.
articles.body:
MERRITT ISLAND — In the playoffs, a series of individual plays could make all the difference of advancing or going home.

That was on full display on Nov. 6 for Merritt Island Christian in the SSAA 8-man state playoffs versus reigning state runner-up Bradenton Christian.

The top-seeded Cougars fell behind by double-digits early, rallied to take the lead only for Bradenton Christian to have a shot to win it on the final possession.

In a game featuring 101 total points, it was the Cougars defense that made the biggest play of the game stopping Bradenton Christian 20 yards short of a game-winning touchdown in a 51-50 win.

"I can't even begin to tell you how proud I am of this team," Merritt Island Christian head coach Josh Babin said. "Every single player, whether they're a starter or a role player, they're phenomenal. It's just been an amazing season."

In a high-scoring game, Merritt Island Christian's defense made some timely stops. The Cougars forced three turnovers on downs with two leading to touchdowns and one preserving a lead.

"It's bend, but don't break. We knew they were going to score. I think the thing that impresses me most about this team, especially (tonight), is nobody gave up," Babin said. "Nobody hung their heads. Nobody said, 'Oh we're down again and it's over.' They all fought through it. They rose above everything. They're a great team, great bunch of kids."

With the Cougars trailing 28-25 in the first half, they forced a four-and-out to get the ball back at their own 40-yard line. Just two plays later, senior Maddux Martinson rushed for a 50-yard touchdown with 4:28 left in the second quarter.

Bradenton Christian drove the ball to the Cougars 5-yard line in the final minute of the first half. Merritt Island Christian stopped the Panthers on four consecutive plays, including a tackle for loss by eighth grader Waylon Perkins on 4th-and-goal. That kept the Cougars in the lead at halftime.

"We had a long talk at halftime. There was a different look in their eye (tonight)," Babin said. "It wasn't the we're not sure what to do. Everybody knew what they needed to do and they did it. It was the most hyped I've seen this team."

In the second half, Bradenton Christian was threatening just outside the red zone leading 34-32 in the third quarter. On a 4th-and-2 at the Cougars 22-yard line, junior Mason Van Slyke wrapped up Panthers freshman Cohen Fuller for a loss of 8 yards.

Merritt Island Christian answered with a go-ahead 11-yard touchdown run by junior Korbin Kugler that put the Cougars in the lead for good.

"There's so many plays. You can dissect the whole game and if that one play doesn't happen, it could be a completely different outcome," Babin said. "I mean our kicker (Brighton Sadler). This is a first-year kicker. No pressure. All the extra points, field goal. Those are difference makers in the game."

It was a fast start for the Merritt Island Christian scoring two plays into the game, but the team went on and fell behind 22-10. They took the lead only for Bradenton Christian to regain the lead on a pick six.

Martinson rebounded from the turnover and guided the Cougars to the comeback win throwing for 214 yards and two touchdowns and rushing for 58 yards and two touchdowns.

"It was a dog fight. It was a back-and-forth battle," Martinson said. "The quarterback was picking us apart, but we were picking them apart in the pass and the run. It was just a fight to the end."

After falling behind 22-10, Martinson threw two touchdowns to senior John Hey for a total of 123 yards. On a 4th-and-inches at the 2-yard line, Martinson reached the end zone on a QB sneak to give the Cougars a 44-34 lead with 4:18 remaining in regulation.

"We just have no quit in this team. No one had their head down. Our coaches, all of our players were just telling us to keep our heads up and we just kept on fighting," Martinson said. "Even after some interceptions and turnovers, we just kept on fighting. Even if we got hurt, the backups still did their job."

Kugler led the rushing attack with 18 carries and one reception for 204 total yards and three touchdowns. The junior scored the final Cougars touchdown on a 20-yard run following a successful stop on a Bradenton Christian onside kick attempt.

"(Kugler's) amazing. He doesn't stop," Martinson said. "He gets hurt and he comes back a couple plays later and he just keeps on fighting. He's played through sickness. He's hurt. It's amazing."

The Cougars played their first down-to-the-wire game of the season after winning their first 11 games by an average margin of 28 points. Babin said this experience couldn't have come at a better time.

"I talked to the boys at the end of the season and I said I wished we would have had a close game," Babin said. "You guys need to know what it is and you need to experience that. It's coming right now and to pull it out with the win, couldn't have asked for a better scenario than this."

Merritt Island Christian extended its state semifinal appearance streak to four years in a row. The Cougars are seeking to win their first state championship since 2023.

"It's something that our coaches didn't think we had at the start of the season, but we've gone on they had more confidence in us and they saw how the new people started to just have that dog in them," Martinson said.

The Cougars will host the No. 4 seed Sports Leadership & Management Academy on Nov. 13. SLAM defeated the No. 5 seed First Academy (Leesburg) 39-21 in the state quarterfinals.

"We've got to stay focused, stay locked in. I'm extremely hard on these guys and that is so we can achieve our ultimate goal of winning a state championship. They understand. We had a little discussion that it's going to be a tough week of practice," Babin said. "Some guys may have to start playing both ways. We may not have the luxury of a true offense and a true defense. Whatever we need to do win the game next week is what we're going to do and then if we're blessed enough to win, we'll carry that on into the state championship game."

For the second year in a row, Satellite loses in the state quarterfinals, putting an end to one of its best seasons in school history. The Scorpions finish the year 10-1 and they graduate 20 seniors.

SSAA Atlantic consolation state quarterfinals

The Bears fall at home to finish the season 6-6 and they graduate 13 seniors. It's the most wins Bayside has posted in a single season since 2014.

articles.title: Silas Demary Jr is ‘having a lot of fun’ with UConn Huskies after win over Michigan
articles.summary: Silas Demary Jr. is enjoying life with UConn after putting up a strong performance in the No. 4 Huskies’ 85-77 win over the No. 16 Michigan Wolverines on Fri...
articles.body:
Silas Demary Jr. is enjoying life with UConn after putting up a strong performance in the No. 4 Huskies' 85-77 win over the No. 16 Michigan Wolverines on Friday night.

Demary has been playing college basketball since 2023, going through his second season with the Huskies. This marks his senior campaign, making it his last chance to shine on the national stage and grow his stock for the NBA level.

Demary certainly came through with a big night against the reigning champions Michigan, who UConn lost to in the national championship game. In 36 minutes of action, he delivered a stat line of 21 points, seven rebounds, four assists, and two steals. He shot 7-of-17 from the field, including 2-of-4 from beyond the arc, and 5-of-7 from the free-throw line.

Demary reflected on the win after the game on the TNT broadcast. Having his teammates surround him in celebration, the standout player made a clear declaration on his enjoyment being part of the winning program.

"I'm having a lot of fun… more fun to come soon," Demary said.

How Silas Demary Jr., UConn played against Michigan

Silas Demary Jr. looks forward to having his senior campaign be as great as it can be. Leading UConn to serious contention for the national championship would be a great feat for the senior star.

Beating Michigan was a great step in the right direction for No. 4 UConn. They set the tone in the first half, outmatching the Wolverines 43-30 once halftime came around.

Three players scored in double-digits for UConn in the win, including Demary. Braylon Mullins led the team with 23 points, four rebounds and one steal. He shot 5-of-12 overall, including 3-of-8 from downtown, and 11-of-12 from the charity stripe. Colben Landrew came next with 14 points and eight rebounds, while Jayden Ross provided nine points and four rebounds.

The No. 4 Huskies will look forward to their next matchup, being at home. They host the Wagner Seahawks as tip-off commences on Nov. 9 at 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Buatsi v Hutchinson 2 - world light-heavyweight title fight predictions
articles.summary: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Saturday's light-heavyweight world title fight between Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson.
articles.body:
Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson renew their rivalry for the vacant WBC world light-heavyweight title in Manchester on Saturday.

The British rivals first met in a highly entertaining, hard-fought contest on the undercard of Daniel Dubois' win over Anthony Joshua in September 2024.

Londoner Buatsi, 33, twice knocked down Hutchinson before going on to win by split decision.

Scotland's Hutchinson, 28, suffered the second defeat of his professional career that night but two wins since have put him in a position to fight for a first world title.

Can Buatsi repeat his victory? Or will Hutchinson gain revenge in Manchester?

BBC Sport spoke to figures from across the boxing world to get their predictions.

Chantelle Cameron - two-weight world champion

"Buatsi may stop him this time in the later rounds. I think he gets it done between rounds nine and 12."

"Willy has improved massively since the first fight, whereas I'm not sure I could say the same for Joshua."

"It's a really good fight. I think the first fight was very good - Willy was dropped a couple of times in the fight and that cost him. Otherwise, his performance was OK. He's matured a lot since that fight and is in good form.

"Buatsi has maybe just started to look old but the fact the world title is on the line... When he turned professional, everyone thought he was a shoo-in to become world champion and he hasn't achieved it yet. This is the chance, so we may see a level of Buatsi that we haven't seen in a while.

"I think it'll be really competitive but I'm just edging Hutchinson to win on points with the run of form he's on."

Viddal Riley - European cruiserweight champion

"Willy Hutchinson will get the win - it's his time. Buatsi is a tough fighter and it won't be easy but when I look at who is fresh and who has the bit between their teeth a little more - I'm backing Hutchinson."

Denzel Bentley - former WBO middleweight champion

"I'm going for a repeat for Buatsi and he finally gets his hands on a world title. It has been 10 years since he was at the Olympics and it felt like he slipped away from that batch of fighters.

"Buatsi does things in his own time and he's finally got his shot. It comes at a great time for him, it could go two ways - he's either overconfident because he's beaten Willy or his confidence could be a good thing and he could step on it early and I think it's the second one.

"I can't see Willy getting stopped - he's tough - so I'm going Buatsi on points, but he might get a knockdown."

Tony Bellew - former cruiserweight world champion

"It's very rare people can turn the rematch around when they lose the first one. On that basis, I am going for Joshua Buatsi, possibly even by late stoppage."

Zelfa Barrett - former European super-featherweight champion

"I'm going with Buatsi to win again. Hutchinson showed he was weak to the body and that could be his kryptonite.

"Hutchinson is a good fighter; he's slick and sharp, but I think Buatsi has his number and wins on points."

"Willy Hutchinson is in his physical and mental prime and I think he wins the fight. I've known Willy since he turned professional as an 18-year-old.

"He's always had the tools to be a world champion and I believe timing is everything in boxing. I believe he's also catching Buatsi at the right time."

Darren Barker - former middleweight world champion

"What a rematch. He showed his worth, his bottle and his ability did Willy Hutchinson in that first fight and proved a lot as a fighter.

"Joshua Buatsi had a very good fight with Callum Smith, although he came out second best. Not so impressive in his win over Zach Parker, it was a close fight so a lot of questions surround him and what's left.

"Hutchinson is a man in form and looks like a man who is matured both physically and mentally. This is a fantastic rematch with the WBC light-heavyweight title on the line. It promises to be an action-packed contest and the pot of gold is massive."

"A rematch that I didn't think would come around but it all makes sense with the added incentive of gold. Someone will leave as world champion. The first time they fought, it was 80-20 Buatsi for me, but Hutchinson was a lot better than I expected.

"He has now closed that gap drastically and now it's 55-45 Buatsi. How much has Callum Smith taken out of Buatsi? On the flip side, Hutchinson, after that defeat, has gone from strength to strength.

"He showed everything in his last fight against Ezra Taylor. I favour Buatsi just, but we'll see how much that Smith fight took out of him. I think Buatsi will be world champion, but I wouldn't be surprised if Willy Hutchinson walks home with gold."

articles.title: Doncic’s 53 points lift Lakers as Cavs top Sixers in LeBron James’s return
articles.summary: LA Lakers star Doncic closed the first half with an astonishing shot from well beyond the half-court line.
articles.body:
Luka Doncic poured in 53 points to propel the Los Angeles Lakers to a 124-118 NBA Cup group-stage victory over Portland on Friday as LeBron James’s latest return to Cleveland ended in defeat.

Doncic’s latest big game helped the Lakers shake off a sluggish start that saw them trailing by as many as 16 points in the second quarter.

Doncic closed the first half with an astonishing shot from well beyond the half-court line, pulling the Lakers within seven points and setting the tone for their second-half surge.

The Trail Blazers had pulled within four points in the final minute when he hit a floater, and the Lakers held on for their fourth straight win.

Doncic has scored at least 40 points in six of his last seven games and joined Elgin Baylor, Kobe Bryant and George Mikan as the only Lakers players to score 40 or more in four straight regular-season contests.

“I’m having a lot of fun,” said Doncic, who added five rebounds and five assists.

“Obviously playing basketball, it’s a lot of fun for me. It’s more [fun] when you play like this and when you win games.”

The 11th 50-point game of Doncic’s career was his fourth with the Lakers – passing LeBron James and tying Mikan for the fourth most for the franchise.

James, who left the Lakers for the Philadelphia 76ers in June, made his first trip as a Sixer to Cleveland, where the Cavs spoiled his latest homecoming with a 119-95 victory that snapped Philadelphia’s five-game winning streak.

James, expected by many to opt for a third stint in Cleveland before he chose Philadelphia, was greeted by warm cheers – and scattered boos – when he was introduced.

The four-time NBA champion, playing his 24th NBA season at the age of 41, was cheered again when he exited the game late in the fourth quarter.

LeBron: ‘I did not feel in good rhythm offensively’

In between, it was a rough night for James and his teammates.

The league’s all-time leading scorer finished with eight points on three-of-12 shooting with seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and six turnovers.

Star centre Joel Embiid missed all nine of his shots from the floor, making six free throws for six points.

Jaylen Brown, like James an off-season import, led the Sixers with 20 points, but the Cavaliers seized control early and repelled every Philadelphia surge.

Donovan Mitchell scored 10 of his 23 points in the first quarter. Evan Mobley added 22 points, and Cleveland out-rebounded Philadelphia 56-42 despite the injury absence of centre Jarrett Allen.

“I did not feel in a good rhythm offensively,” James said.

“We didn’t look like much offensively. We had a couple of spurts. We were able to cut [the deficit] to three in the third quarter. But too many turnovers on my behalf.”

Friday’s games were part of NBA Cup group-stage action, which will continue throughout November.

Quarterfinals of the in-season tournament will be played December 4-5 and semifinals December 8-9 before the final on December 11.

The Boston Celtics drained a whopping 24 three-pointers on 44 attempts in a 119-80 blowout of the Hornets in Charlotte.

Jayson Tatum drilled five three-pointers on the way to a game-high 34 points for Boston, who led by as many as 46 in the wire-to-wire win.

San Antonio star Victor Wembanyama, coming off a stunning 52-point, 24-rebound performance in a win over Dallas, scored 30 points and pulled down 14 rebounds to lead the Spurs to a 124-109 victory over the Kings in Sacramento.

The Oklahoma City Thunder continued their dominance of the Grizzlies with a 128-97 win in Memphis.

Ajay Mitchell scored a career-high 35 points, and two-time defending NBA Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander added 28 for the Thunder, who notched a 13th straight regular-season win over the Grizzlies despite missing injured starters Jaylen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren.

The absences were irrelevant as the Thunder jumped to a 71-49 halftime lead.

articles.title: Franco Colapinto Drives the Alpine-Themed Renault 6 Fans Took From Argentina to Brazil
articles.summary: Franco Colapinto has just shared a special moment with a group of fans who traveled from Argentina to Brazil to support him. The fans had…
articles.body:
Franco Colapinto has just shared a special moment with a group of fans who traveled from Argentina to Brazil to support him. The fans had restored a 1977 Renault 6 and decorated it with Alpine's signature blue, pink and white colors, along with Colapinto's racing number 43. Their remarkable journey from Esperanza, Santa Fe, to Brazil covered more than 2,000 kilometers.

The three fans, Hernán Bonvín, Claudio Goddio and Pablo Quaino, had set out on the adventure with the dream of meeting their Formula 1 hero. After spotting the uniquely decorated car, Colapinto greeted the group with a smile and took a closer look at their creation.

What followed was an unforgettable surprise as the Alpine driver climbed behind the wheel and took the Renault 6 for a drive through the streets of São Paulo.

Videos of the encounter quickly spread across social media, capturing Colapinto enjoying the experience while the excited fans cheered from inside the vehicle.

The Argentine even joked about the car's radio system, asking whether it worked as he drove, prompting laughter from his passengers. The light-hearted interaction offered a memorable glimpse of the connection between the young driver and his supporters.

Seeing Colapinto drive the car they had worked months on to get going made it all worth their while. The car, which they named 'Renoleta ', became an eye-catching wonder wherever it went. It became an even more significant deal for the Argentine driver during the Brazilian GP weekend, as it highlighted the enthusiasm of South American F1 supporters.

Franco Colapinto Has Reignited Argentina's F1 Passion

Colapinto has rapidly become one of the most well-known young faces in Argentine motorsport, and his arrival in F1 has certainly rekindled the passion for the sport in Argentina. A country with a very strong motorsport tradition, his presence on the grid has been a real boost. His performances, as well as his personability, have really helped him to connect with fans of all ages.

The 23-year-old's rising profile is also a reflection of the renewed interest in F1 amongst the Argentine fans, who have taken him as an ambassador for their country in the world of motorsport.

It's not just on the track that he's been embraced, with a huge amount of social media interaction and genuine passion for him at the race meetings. He's brought the country a lot of international attention.

As he continues to build his career in F1, Colapinto has become a figure of interest for the Argentinian fanbase who are keen to see one of their own make his mark at the top of the sport. His relationship with the fans has become a key part of his public persona, and that in itself is a huge part of the appeal. It's a journey that the next generation of Argentinian F1 fans will follow closely.

Franco Colapinto Fans Can Be a Bit Too Emotional

It is hardly a secret that South American fans take sports very seriously, and things can sometimes escalate to extremities in terms of fandom. While F1 does not have a plethora of examples in this context, one of the most prominent ones came in September, when Colapinto was a primary subject of a multi-car crash in Azerbaijan.

Colapinto lost control of his car in Baku and caused a multi-car pile-up during a safety car restart, taking Lando Norris and Pierre Gasly out of the race.

Without viewing the footage and without naming anyone, Norris suggested that whoever caused the collision should be handed a one-race ban. Taking the comment to heart, Colapinto's fans flooded Norris on social media with a flurry of hate and abuse.

Gasly and a few others also got caught in the crossfire, with Colapinto labeling the behavior as something that was "not nice to see." Alpine subsequently issued a statement in which it condemned the online abuse without pointing to any particular fanbase.

The French outfit felt it was necessary for them to speak up in a difficult time, particularly given that members of the entire F1 community were being targeted.

Ultimately, the team did not want to point fingers at anyone and labeled the crash a racing incident that should be let go by the fans.

articles.title: Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur honors the late Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday with epic t-shirt

articles.body:
Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur made a heartfelt gesture Friday, honoring franchise legend Pat Tillman on what would have been his 50th birthday. LaFleur, who recently made a major quarterback change involving Gardner Minshew, arrived at his media availability wearing a shirt featuring the late safety.

The maroon shirt featured an image of Tillman wearing his No. 40 Cardinals jersey, offering a simple but meaningful tribute photo to one of the organization's most respected figures.

Cardinals reporter Mark Dalton shared a photo of LaFleur's tribute, highlighting the coach's decision to commemorate Tillman's milestone birthday.

Tillman, born November 6, 1976, played college football at Arizona State before joining the Cardinals in 1998. He spent four seasons with Arizona, establishing himself as a hard-hitting safety and earning widespread admiration for his dedication.

Following the September 11 attacks, Tillman made the extraordinary decision to leave professional football and enlist in the United States Army alongside his brother Kevin.

He served as an Army Ranger before passing away in Afghanistan on April 22, 2004, at just 27 years old.

His legacy remains deeply connected to the Cardinals, who retired his No. 40 jersey and erected a statue outside State Farm Stadium in his honor.

The tribute came as LaFleur prepared Arizona for its upcoming matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, with the Cardinals navigating significant roster changes after Jacoby Brissett's departure to the Baltimore Ravens.

Despite the demands of preparing for another divisional contest, LaFleur took time to recognize a figure whose influence extends well beyond football.

His shirt served as another reminder that Tillman's sacrifice and legacy continue to resonate throughout the Cardinals organization.

articles.body:
Cardiff Devils remain top of Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) after a hard-earned 2-1 overtime victory against Dundee Stars at Vindico Arena on Friday, 6 November.

Visiting netminder Vladislav Pestov finished with 53 saves for the Stars who frustrated a dominant home side with a resolute defensive display.

Dundee opened the scoring in the first period through Matthew DeBoer, after a breakaway from a Devils error.

The home side finally found a way through with a Brandon Estes shot from point to equalise midway through the second.

Neither side could force a regulation winner, and there were just 40 seconds left on the clock in overtime when Kristoff Kontos scored his first league goal of the season to claim the extra point for Cardiff.

"It's two points, it's a win," said a relieved Devils head coach Paul Thompson.

"We didn't make the most of the [offensive] zone time that we had from a scoring perspective, but I'm happy that Kontos made that big play to score us the OT winner."

Cardiff - who have 13 points, the same as second placed Sheffield Steelers - travel to Fife Flyers on Sunday, 8 November (17:00 GMT).

articles.title: Olivia Smart y Tim Dieck, bronce en la Copa de China
articles.standfirst: La pareja española logra subir por segunda vez en su carrera al podio de un Grand Prix y mantiene sus opciones de clasificarse para la final
articles.summary: La pareja española logra subir por segunda vez en su carrera al podio de un Grand Prix y mantiene sus opciones de clasificarse para la final
articles.body: Olivia Smart y Tim Dieck se han estrenado esta temporada en el Grand Prix con una medalla de bronce en la Copa de China, tercera cita de este prestigioso circuito organizado por la Unión Internacional de Patinaje (ISU). La pareja española sumó un total de 178,30 puntos, una puntuación que le permitió remontar desde la quinta posición que ocupaba tras la danza rítmica disputada el viernes. Se trata de la segunda vez que suben al podio en una prueba del Grand Prix, después de conseguirlo en el Skate America de 2024. Con 'Enigma', uno de los montajes más originales y difíciles del panorama internacional, salieron este sábado al hielo del Shenzhen Universiade Center con el objetivo de escalar posiciones. Un percance en la elevación de la danza rítmica, unido a una penalización en el elemento coreográfico, les había relegado a la quinta posición. Un resultado provisional decepcionante para una pareja que aspiraba a luchar por la victoria. Lo sucedido el viernes les pasó factura y este sábado patinaron algo tensos y precavidos. Esto se hizo evidente en una poco habitual pérdida de coordinación en el set de twizzles, que fue penalizada por el panel técnico. Las tres elevaciones, todas ellas realmente creativas, fueron excelentes, al igual que la pirueta. Ejecutaron con bastante corrección las dos secuencias de pasos e interpretaron magníficamente la secuencia coreográfica. Cerraron su programa con la elevación coreográfica, un movimiento realmente arriesgado al que en esta ocasión le faltó algo de fluidez. Algo comprensible a estas alturas de la temporada, especialmente tratándose de una figura de extraordinaria complejidad. Con un poco más de rodaje en los ejercicios, Smart y Dieck pueden optar a todo esta temporada. Obtuvieron 107,32 puntos en la danza libre, para un total acumulado de 178,30, lo que les permitió hacerse con la medalla de bronce por apenas 0,09 puntos. La victoria fue para los británicos Lilah Fear y Lewis Gibson, con un total de 194,93 puntos, mientras que la plata correspondió a los georgianos Diana Davis y Gleb Smolkin, con 193,54. "No estamos demasiado satisfechos. Ambos estábamos nerviosos antes de salir al hielo para el programa libre y, después de un día como el de ayer, es comprensible. Sentimos que hoy hemos hecho nuestro trabajo, pero todavía tenemos mucho que entrenar y mejorar en este programa", afirmó Olivia Smart. Con este resultado, suman 11 puntos para el ranking del Grand Prix. Su presencia en la final, uno de los grandes objetivos de esta temporada, dependerá de su actuación en el NHK Trophy, que disputarán del 27 al 29 de noviembre en Tokio (Japón). "Vamos a aprovechar al máximo estas dos próximas semanas hasta el NHK Trophy, exigiremos lo máximo de nosotros mismos y esperamos que, con los resultados que consigamos en el NHK, podamos clasificarnos para la final", añadió Smart.

articles.title: India beat New Zealand by four runs via DLS in rain-hit second ODI
articles.summary: Put in to bat, New Zealand struggled to gain any momentum as ⁠India’s pace attack dismantled their batting lineup.
articles.body:
India’s seam bowlers thrived in helpful conditions for a second straight one-day international as they beat New Zealand by four runs on Saturday to take a 2-0 series lead.

New Zealand were unable to defend their total of 134, with wet conditions in Wellington having reduced game two to a maximum of 47 overs each and made batting conditions treacherous.

India were 113-7 off 26 overs when rain ended play, four runs ahead of the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern par score of 109.

KL Rahul was at the crease on 26 and Auqib Nabi on one, with the pair having done just enough to put the tourists in front.

They require one more win to wrap up the five-match series, heading into game three in Hamilton on Tuesday.

India won the rain-hit opener in Auckland on Wednesday by five wickets when the home side were skittled for 185.

They were never comfortable in their Wellington chase, rocked onto the back foot when New Zealand seamer Jacob Duffy (3-35) dismissed Indian captain Shubman Gill for a golden duck and Virat Kohli for seven.

Paceman Kyle Jamieson (3-35) made a key breakthrough by removing top-scorer Shreyas Iyer for 30, leaving the chase teetering at 86-5.

New Zealand were all out in 41 overs, led by a watchful 55 from Daryl Mitchell and 31 from captain Mitchell Santner.

No other home batsman scored more than 11, many of them undone by unpredictable bounce and tight Indian seam bowling.

Gurnoor Brar produced his best ODI figures of 4-30, making a key double-strike in the 20th over when he removed Tom Latham and Glenn Phillips cheaply to leave New Zealand 53-5.

Earlier, Auqib Nabi claimed his first two international wickets, taking openers Will Young and Tim Seifert to finish with 2-31.

articles.title: 6 Terrible Contracts NHL Teams Wish Would Disappear
articles.summary: The NHL's salary cap has, with few exceptions, steadily risen since it was implemented in 2005. From $39 million in 2005-06, it's currently at $104 million for 2026-27 and will rise to $113.5 million for 2027-28.
articles.body:
The NHL's salary cap has, with few exceptions, steadily risen since it was implemented in 2005. From $39 million in 2005-06, it's currently at $104 million for 2026-27 and will rise to $113.5 million for 2027-28 .

As the cap rises, so does player salaries as teams use the extra cap dollars to re-sign key players or to bolster their rosters through free agency. It often leads to top talent signing expensive long-term contracts.

In some cases, those contracts will pan out over the long term. In others, teams can end up signing players for far more than their worth.

In those cases, it's because a player isn't achieving the same level of success with a new team as he did with his former club.

Sometimes, it's because a general manager overvalued the player's worth when signing him.

It can also be due to a player struggling to meet expectations that come with an expensive new contract.

Whatever the reason for those bad contracts, they affect the market for players seeking new deals, driving them higher.

Here's a look at six contracts that NHL clubs wish would disappear.

On July 22, 2022, the Calgary Flames acquired Jonathan Huberdeau as part of the return for sending winger Matthew Tkachuk to the Florida Panthers. Two weeks later, they signed Huberdeau to an eight-year contract with an average annual value of $10.5 million.

The trade became one of this decade's most lopsided moves. Tkachuk helped the Panthers reach the Stanley Cup Final in three straight years, winning back-to-back championships in 2024 and 2025.

Huberdeau, meanwhile, never regained the offensive heights he reached with the Panthers, including a career-best 115-point campaign in 2021-22. His highest output with the Flames was a 62-point effort in 2024-25.

While Huberdeau's numbers were respectable, they definitely weren't what was expected of a player earning his salary. One reason was that the Flames weren't as talented as the Panthers. Another was a nagging hip condition that shortened his 2025-26 season and has kept him sidelined thus far this season.

The sharp rise of the salary cap and the Flames' current rebuilding process make his contract less burdensome for the club. Nevertheless, the 33-year-old left winger is unlikely to return to the high-scoring form of his days with the Panthers. He remains among the league's most overpaid players.

On July 1, 2024, the Boston Bruins made one of the summer's biggest signings, inking Elias Lindholm to a seven-year, $54.25 million contract . He was the top center in the market that year and was expected to fill the void left by the retirements of long-time Bruins centers Patrice Bergeron and David Krejci.

Lindholm wasn't a superstar like Bergeron. Nevertheless, his strong two-way game made him a star during his five-plus seasons with the Calgary Flames. That included three seasons with 64-plus points, including a career-high 82 points in 2021-22.

However, Lindholm struggled to regain his solid two-way game during his first two seasons with the Bruins. He saw time on the top-two lines, including with superstar winger David Pastrnak, but his production was below 50 points, although an injury hampered his performance last season.

The 31-year-old Lindholm has shown promising improvement so far this season, sitting second among the Bruins with 14 points. However, if his production drops off again and his defensive struggles return, his contract will continue to be a regrettable one for Bruins management.

Days before the March 3, 2023 NHL trade deadline, the New Jersey Devils made one of the biggest moves of 2022-23. On Feb. 26, they acquired winger Timo Meier from the San Jose Sharks in a multi-player deal usually seen during the offseason in today's salary-cap world.

Four months later, the Devils signed Meier, who was slated to become a restricted free agent that summer, to an eight-year contract worth an average annual value of $8.8 million.

At the time, it seemed like a good deal. Meier was (and still is) a physical, versatile two-way forward who can play either wing. He reached the 30-goal plateau twice and had a career-high 40 goals split between the Devils and San Jose Sharks in '22-'23.

However, Meier's production has declined since joining the Devils. He's still among their top-six forwards , but he's not producing at the level expected of a power forward with his annual salary. At his current pace, his contract will not age well over the remaining term.

From the day Darnell Nurse signed his eight-year, $74 million contract with the Edmonton Oilers on Aug. 6, 2021, the team's fans increasingly wished it would disappear. A solid second-pairing defenseman, he put up decent offensive numbers, but he wasn't going to reach the level expected of a top-pairing defenseman .

Oilers fans got their wish on July 1, when the Oilers traded Nurse and his $9.25 million average annual value through 2029-30 to the San Jose Sharks. Lacking experienced blueline depth, the Sharks had the cap space to take on his contract, hoping that he could improve their defense.

The Sharks still have plenty of projected salary-cap space going forward with Nurse on their payroll. They obviously valued the veteran presence and leadership that he was bringing to their young blue line.

However, Nurse is still plagued by the defensive issues that drew criticism during his Edmonton days. Now 31, any hope that a change of scenery could improve his performance will likely fade as the season goes on, which could leave Sharks fans wishing his contract would go away.

When the Vancouver Canucks signed Elias Pettersson to an eight-year extension on March 2, 2024, he was considered an emerging young superstar worthy of an $11.6 million average annual value.

Pettersson had a career-high 102-point performance in 2022-23, and while his production dropped to 89 points the following season, he was still considered an elite player. His strong two-way play helped the Canucks finish that season with their third-best record in franchise history (109 points).

Over the next two years, however, Pettersson's performance declined significantly, partly because he was clashing with teammate J.T. Miller. Trading Miller to the New York Rangers in January 2025 did nothing to help Pettersson regain his form.

Now 27, Pettersson has improved this season , averaging a point per game with the rebuilding Canucks. Whether he maintains that effort throughout this season remains to be seen.

Pettersson's improvement might entice another club to make a reasonable trade offer to the Canucks. If so, they could jump on it to bring in young assets that fit within their rebuilding plans while clearing his contract from their books.

The Seattle Kraken signed Chandler Stephenson on July 1, 2024, to a seven-year contract with a $6.25 million average annual value. They hoped the two-time Stanley Cup champion would provide experienced depth and scoring to their top-six forward lines.

At the time, Stephenson was coming off a solid three-year stretch with the Vegas Golden Knights. Frequently skating alongside stars like Mark Stone, Jack Eichel, and Jonathan Marchessault, he had two seasons with 64-65 points and a 51-point campaign in 2023-24.

However, he wasn't skating with players of that caliber with the Kraken, and he hasn't regained the 65-point level he had during his best seasons in Las Vegas. His defensive game also suffered.

On a better team, Stephenson would be a third-line forward. On the offensively anemic Kraken, he's being paid like a second-liner, but he has struggled over the past two years to meet the expectations that come with his contract.

Stephenson is off to a good start this season, with 12 points while skating on the Kraken's second line . However, he's now 32, and it's unlikely he can maintain that pace for long.

articles.title: YangWang Altior: el descomunal coche eléctrico con el que BYD quiere conquistar el mundo del lujo
articles.standfirst: El Yangwang Altior es una imponente limusina de 5,60 metros, con cuatro motores eléctricos, un interior digno de una suite presidencial y tecnología capaz de hacerla girar sobre sí misma
articles.summary: El Yangwang Altior es una imponente limusina de 5,60 metros, con cuatro motores eléctricos, un interior digno de una suite presidencial y tecnología capaz de hacerla girar sobre sí misma
articles.body: BYD quiere demostrar que los fabricantes chinos también pueden competir en el escalón más alto del lujo automovilístico. De ahí que haya elegido una de las cunas del mundo de la exclusividad, Abu Dhabi, para presentar al mundo el nuevo Altior, una espectacular limusina eléctrica con la que pretende llevar su tecnología a un terreno tradicionalmente dominado por marcas como Rolls-Royce, Bentley o Mercedes-Maybach. En MARCA hemos podido asistir a su espectacular puesta de largo en el Palacio Presidencial de Abu Dhabi y hay que reconocer que en vivo impone. Estamos ante un automóvil de 5,60 metros de longitud, con un habitáculo para que cuatro ocupantes viajen a cuerpo de rey, materiales exclusivos, una autonomía que supera los 1.000 kilómetros y algunas soluciones tecnológicas que parecen propias de la ciencia ficción. Como la posibilidad de girar sobre sí mismo o la de mantenerse a flote en una situación de emergencia. Algo de lo que ya son capaces otros modelos de la marca de lujo de BYD. El Altior no es precisamente un coche discreto. Sus 5.600 mm de longitud, 2.030 mm de anchura y 1.590 mm de altura lo colocan entre las berlinas de representación más grandes del mundo. Su distancia entre ejes, de nada menos que 3,50 metros, permite reservar un espacio extraordinario para los ocupantes. Para su diseño, en el que se ha trabajado durante tres años, Yangwang dice haber buscado inspiración en el ding, un antiguo recipiente chino de bronce. Esa influencia se aprecia en las formas contundentes de su carrocería y en un frontal casi vertical, con una parrilla que recuerda a una pieza de alta joyería. Incluso su iluminación tiene algo de espectáculo: 12 elementos luminosos se activan secuencialmente cuando el propietario se aproxima al vehículo. Las puertas también están pensadas para facilitar una entrada casi ceremonial: las delanteras se abren hasta 80 grados y las posteriores hasta 90. Y, como detalle propio de las grandes berlinas de lujo, incorpora paraguas hechos a medida integrados en las puertas. Pero donde realmente pretende marcar diferencias el Altior es en su habitáculo, concebido para que los pasajeros traseros sean los auténticos protagonistas. Solo hay cuatro plazas, con dos enormes asientos posteriores de 'gravedad cero', (la denominación que utilizan los fabricantes chinos para los que incluyen varias reclinaciones y climatización) reposapiernas y un avanzado sistema de masaje mecánico. El espacio tampoco debería ser un problema, con 1.209 mm para las piernas de los ocupantes posteriores. Además, con solo pulsar un botón, el asiento del acompañante delantero puede plegarse para despejar la visión del pasajero que viaja detrás... y maximizar su confort. El lujo está presente en todos los detalles: cuero semianilina, alfombrillas de lana pura, maderas naturales, auténtico jade amarillo de Hetian (una gema muy apreciada en China) y bordados artesanales de Suzhou.(una localidad famosa por cultivar este arte popular) Incluso los mandos metálicos se han desarrollado prestando especial atención al sonido y las sensaciones que transmiten al accionarlos. Y la tecnología no se queda atrás. El YangWang Altior equipa un sistema de sonido Dynaudio Platinum Evidence con 39 altavoces, una pantalla de 21,4 pulgadas que se eleva eléctricamente y dos frigoríficos, uno delante y otro detrás. El posterior, con 5,5 litros de capacidad, permite tanto enfriar como calentar su contenido. También dispone de un modo de relajación que, mediante una sola pulsación, reclina los asientos, eleva los reposapiernas, cierra las persianas y ajusta la iluminación, la música, la climatización aromática y activa los masajes para crear un ambiente de descanso. Con todo este despliegue de confort, casi que lo de menos es la mecánica. Pero debajo esa carrocería se esconde otra de las grandes bazas de BYD: su tecnología eléctrica. El Altior utiliza la plataforma e4, con cuatro motores eléctricos independientes, uno encargado de controlar la fuerza motriz en cada rueda. El sistema puede realizar ajustes más de 100 veces por segundo para optimizar la estabilidad y el comportamiento. Esta configuración permite algunas maniobras poco habituales en un automóvil de semejante tamaño, como girar prácticamente sobre su propio eje. También incorpora una función de flotación de emergencia (que en su día incluso pudimos experimentar en el YangWang U8) para situaciones en las que el vehículo acabe accidentalmente sumergido en agua. La suspensión inteligente DiSus trabaja conjuntamente con los motores para controlar los movimientos de la carrocería (una labor ardua en un mastodonte de este tonelaje) y anticiparse a las irregularidades de la carretera, buscando el máximo confort de marcha. Además, utiliza la segunda generación de la batería Blade de BYD, que le permite anunciar más de 1.000 kilómetros de autonomía en el ciclo de homologación chino CLTC, una cifra que, ojo, sólo debe servirnos como referencia porque no es directamente comparable con las WLTP europeas. También contará con la nueva tecnología de carga ultrarrápida FLASH Charging, aunque la marca todavía no ha comunicado sus prestaciones concretas. El Altior estrena asimismo el procesador Xuanji A3 de 4 nanómetros, desarrollado por BYD, que gestiona su avanzado sistema de asistencia a la conducción God's Eye A, con funciones de asistencia para circular por ciudad, autopista y aparcar. El nuevo Yangwang Altior se ofrecerá en dos variantes, Executive y Bespoke, esta última con mayores posibilidades de personalización. La marca también ha anunciado una primera edición especial limitada, denominada Shanhe Dingyun, que combina tonos exteriores marrones y dorados con un interior inspirado en el jade. Por el momento, BYD no ha anunciado el precio de su nueva berlina de representación ni ha confirmado los mercados en los que estará disponible (por tanto, nos quedamos con la duda de si lo veremos en Europa). Lo que sí parece claro es que, con el Altior, el fabricante chino quiere demostrar que su ambición no termina en los eléctricos populares: también aspira a conquistar a los clientes más exigentes del mundo
