articles.title: Gemma Triay y Paula Josemaría dan a España el décimo Mundial femenino de su historia
articles.standfirst: La balear y la extremeña doblegaron a Claudia Jensen y Delfi Brea en el segundo punto, necesitando tres sets, y confirmando el dominio nacional con el séptimo entorchado consecutivo
articles.summary: La balear y la extremeña doblegaron a Claudia Jensen y Delfi Brea en el segundo punto, necesitando tres sets, y confirmando el dominio nacional con el séptimo entorchado consecutivo
articles.body: Se cumplieron los pronósticos. España se proclama campeona del mundo de pádel en categoría femenina en 2026 tras ganarle la final a Argentina. Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero pusieron el primer punto para que Gemma Triay y Paula Josemaría remataran la faena con un 2-0 que pone el séptimo título consecutivo en las vitrinas de ‘La Roja’, el décimo en total. Un nuevo éxito para el pádel nacional, que sigue creciendo con su generación dorada. La semana fue plácida para el Dream Team español. Prácticamente todas las mejores jugadoras del mundo estaban presentes en la convocatoria para formar el que, en palabras de la seleccionadora, es el mejor equipo de la historia del país. Hasta la final, el camino transcurrió sin problemas, pero debían cumplir con su favoritismo ante unas argentinas que siempre tiran de garra y que amenazaban con complicar el cuento de ensueño que vivían las de Carolina. Ari Sánchez y Andrea Ustero se llevaron el primer partido sin problemas. La dupla catalana aprovechó su gran momento de forma para doblegar a Aranza Osoro y Martina Fassio con un doble 6-3. La ‘Vikinga’ tuvo destellos que parecían igualar la contienda, pero la dupla número tres del mundo no se dejó intimidar. La drive zurda reconoció estar nerviosa al terminar, pero en todo momento tuvieron el dominio del encuentro para dejar a España a un solo paso de ganar. El siguiente punto fue para Paula Josemaría y Gemma Triay. Una pareja que, si bien nunca había competido junta, ofrecía garantías de sobra por su experiencia y trayectoria. Y así fue. Delante estaban Delfi Brea y Claudia Jensen, las dos principales figuras de Argentina que ya venían compitiendo codo con codo en anteriores rondas. Tiraron de garra y lo pelearon hasta el final, poniendo en serios aprietos a Gemma y Paula, pero finalmente la menorquina y la extremeña cerraron el partido para darle el título a España. Arrancaron mucho mejor Triay y Josemaría. Recital de las hispanas en los primeros compases, rindiendo a un nivel espectacular que puso el 6-2 en el luminoso. Parecía un camino de rosas, pero las argentinas pusieron todo su corazón y pasión en la pista para igualar las sensaciones. Una Brea cambiada de lado sacó su mejor versión para evidenciar que su número uno no es casualidad. Además, con polémica, pues hubo una serie de warnings que alteraron el transcurso de un partido que parecía sencillo para Paula y Gemma. Tuvieron incluso bola de set Delfi y Claudia, pero sin poder hacerla efectiva, por lo que todo se fue a la muerte súbita. Cuando la tensión estaba en su punto máximo, en el tie-break, las argentinas dieron un recital, aprovechando también los errores de las rivales. Saltó la sorpresa momentánea, llevándolo al tercer set gracias al 7-6. Saltaban las alarmas en el banquillo español. El tercero siguió con mucha igualdad y muchas dificultades para Josemaría y Triay, aunque poco a poco se volvieron a hacer dueñas y señoras del choque. La drive empezó a fallar menos, mientras que ‘Gemmagnífica’ tomó las riendas en un cruzado épico con su compañera en Premier Padel. Un break fue suficiente para decantar la balanza, ganar el partido con un 6-3 definitivo y proclamar a España campeona del mundo en 2026. No hizo falta que saltaran a la pista Bea y Claudia, que conformaban la tercera dupla de la alineación. Otro Mundial ante Argentina con un equipo compuesto por Andrea Ustero, Ari Sánchez, Martina Calvo, Marta Ortega, Gemma Triay, Paula Josemaría, Claudia Fernández y Bea González. Tras la consecución del título en 2024 en una final que se decidió también por 2-0, España suma su décimo Mundial en categoría femenina y el séptimo consecutivo. Una racha histórica de varias generaciones doradas para el pádel nacional.

articles.summary: The Detroit Lions have three defensive positions to address before the NFL trade deadline, with the defensive line, linebacker and cornerback groups emerging...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions have three defensive positions to address before the NFL trade deadline , with the defensive line, linebacker and cornerback groups emerging as areas of concern. Detroit needs reinforcements to keep pace in the NFC North as its division rivals strengthen their rosters and injuries create additional uncertainty on defense.

articles.title: Catholic Memorial advances to Division 3 football semifinals
articles.summary: Catholic Memorial dominated Whitefish Bay 40-15 to secure a spot in the Division 3 high school football semifinals.
articles.body:
WHITEFISH BAY − Catholic Memorial entered Friday night's Division 3 quarterfinal football matchup against Whitefish Bay as the underdog.

The Crusaders defeated the Blue Dukes, 40-15, using a strong defensive performance and timely scoring to earn a spot in the Division 3 semifinals.

Catholic Memorial (7-5) established control early, scoring 17 unanswered points in the first half. Will Schmitzer opened the scoring with a 34-yard touchdown in the first quarter before the Crusaders added a field goal and another touchdown to take a 17-0 lead into halftime.

Whitefish Bay (9-3) responded in the third quarter with a touchdown from Mace Miskel, cutting the deficit to 17-7. However, Catholic Memorial answered with a 59-yard rushing touchdown to extend its lead to 24-7.

The Crusaders continued to build momentum in the fourth quarter. Ne'Vareon Flowers scored on a 1-yard touchdown run, followed by a successful two-point conversion to make it 32-7.

Scenes from Arrowhead-Sussex Hamilton in a WIAA football quarterfinal

Devon Williams Jr. added another touchdown for Catholic Memorial, and the Crusaders converted another two-point attempt to extend their advantage to 40-7.

Whitefish Bay added a late touchdown and two-point conversion, but the deficit was too much to overcome.

Catholic Memorial head coach Bill Young credited his team's preparation and defensive execution for the victory.

Young specifically praised defensive coordinator Ryan Stefaniak and Steve Rux, along with several players who helped lead the defensive effort, including Dalton Steinke, Dustin Roach, Cam Shumpert, Flowers and Schmitzer.

"We were really dialed in," Young said. "We were battle-tested."

That preparation came from what Young described as one of the toughest schedules in the state. Catholic Memorial faced seven Division 1 opponents and two Division 2 opponents during the regular season.

Young said competing against that level of competition helped establish the standard his team needed to reach heading into the postseason.

"When you get a chance to play against great teams, the bar is set for you," Young said. "It's just a deal that we were ready to compete."

The Crusaders also benefited from a strong week of preparation, including long practices and an extended walkthrough Friday morning.

Catholic Memorial advances to the Division 3 semifinals, moving one step closer to a state championship appearance.

Young knows the competition will only get tougher as the postseason continues.

"At this level, you get to Level 2, Level 3, you're playing great teams, great coaches, great programs," Young said. "You have to dominate and do the little things right, make your block, do your job, great tackling. We did that tonight. Now we've got to get ready for next week."

Catholic Memorial will face Pewaukee on Friday, Nov. 13, in a Division 3 semifinal matchup.

articles.title: Farke hails Leeds’ second-half performance – and gives update on Gudmundsson
articles.summary: Leeds United boss Daniel Farke believes his side were the only team pushing to win the game in the second half as they secured a 1-0 victory over Tottenham H...
articles.body:
Leeds United boss Daniel Farke believes his side were the only team pushing to win the game in the second half as they secured a 1-0 victory over Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road.

After a relatively even opening 45 minutes, Leeds took control following the break with substitute Noah Okafor scoring the winner in the 79th minute.

"There's no replacement for this winning feeling in the dressing room, it's great to have it back," Farke said.

"Terrific performance against an in-form Tottenham side.

"For us it has been a difficult period, we've been missing key players in the offence in training and games, players like Anton Stach, Noah Okafor, Dominic Calvert-Lewin has not had the easiest spell with injury problems.

"It was important to show this unity, commitment and be tactically spot on to avoid their processes and individual quality.

"We reduced them to very little. We were missing a bit in the final third, the finishing pass wasn't there. But in the second half only one team was pushing."

Leeds did suffer an injury concern, though, with Gabriel Gudmundsson forced off at half-time due to a hamstring problem.

"Gabi had problems with his hamstring and it was not possible to keep going," Farke said.

"I always prefer to have him available but Melvin had his best week in training since he came to us.

"You could feel he had momentum and I was not one moment concerned when I had to throw him in.

"Very competitive, very concentrated but it's no coincidence. I'm a big believer that you play like you train.

"I hope it's not too bad with Gabi and hope to have him back for Chelsea, but credit to Melvin he also played his part in a very good second half."

articles.title: Moorhead's historic season comes to an abrupt end with playoff upset loss
articles.summary: The No. 1-ranked team in Minnesota suffered an upset loss on Friday night.
articles.body:
The Moorhead Spuds put together one of the best offensive regular seasons in the history of Minnesota high school football, but their postseason run came to an end with a second-round upset loss, 19-14 to Prior Lake on Friday night at home.

The Spuds were widely viewed as the No. 1 high school football team in the state of Minnesota, but the Lakers handed them a 19-14 loss on their home field to end their season.

Gophers commit QB Jett Feeney was off his game. He finished 11 of 24 for just 128 yards and one touchdown. He had nine carries for 88 yards and one touchdown on the ground, but Prior Lake's defense limited him to his worst game of the season. He also threw his first two interceptions of the entire season.

Fellow Gophers commit wide receiver David Mack was injured in Moorhead's first-round win over Coon Rapids, and the Spuds' offense clearly missed him. Cornerback/wide receiver Zak Walker stepped up in his absence with five catches for 57 yards. Running back Taye Reich, who's also committed to the Gophers, finished with 13 carries for 74 yards.

Feeney, Mack, Reich and Walker's high school careers are now over as key parts of one of the most successful senior classes in the history of Moorhead football. All four are committed to play football at the University of Minnesota, and their next step will be early national signing day in December.

Prior Lake was ready for the moment, and it will now face No. 2 seed Rosemount on Thursday night at Maple Grove in the quarterfinals, with a trip to U.S. Bank Stadium and the Class 6A semifinals on the line. That game is scheduled for 6 p.m. CT.

articles.title: Tottenham dealt latest attacking injury blow after VAR madness at Leeds
articles.summary: VAR spent over four minutes reviewing a possible red card offence when Jayden Bogle stamped on Tel’s ankle, but the challenge - which forced the Frenchman of...
articles.body:
Tottenham have been dealt another attacking injury blow after Mathys Tel limped off before half-time against Leeds .

Tel was unable to continue after being on the end of a stamp by Jayden Bogle, who caught the Frenchman on the ankle with his studs.

VAR spent over four minutes reviewing the incident to determine whether it was a red card offence, only for referee John Brooks - who didn't even caution Bogle initially - to be told to stick with the on-field decision. This meant the right wing-back got away with the challenge scot free.

"The referee's call of no red card to Bogle for the challenge on Tel was checked and confirmed by VAR," said the Premier League Match Centre.

The statement added VAR Tony Harrington's verdict to Brooks: "I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There's a lack of speed going into the challenge and he's stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge".

The challenge was similar to the one that saw Jean-Philippe Mateta shown red after a VAR review when Spurs played Crystal Palace last weekend.

Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi was visibly frustrated with the outcome of the review and expressed his displeasure again when Pedro Porro was booked for a similar foul after the break, with the Italian booked for his reaction.

"Pedro Porro's was a duel and an incredible yellow card. The first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing," De Zerbi told TNT Sports , before stopping short of criticising the officials.

Asked if the referee should have gone to the monitor to review Bogle's challenge, he said: "No. I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor. If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve."

Farke, meanwhile, insisted that Bogle would never have gone into the challenge with ill intent, branding his player a "butterfly".

He said: "I have heard there were several doubtful situations. A possible hand ball. I just know that Jayden Bogle out of any bad intention. It looked like a coming together.

"It's very unlucky outcome that Mathys is injured and we wish him all the best and he can recover quickly. The last thing Jayden Bogle is a nasty player. He's possibly the softest player in the whole league. I always call him my butterfly, and I can guarantee it was never out of bad intention."

De Zerbi's woes were exacerbated when Tel signalled to the bench that he would need to come off, having tried to play through the pain for five minutes.

Tel was replaced by Dominic Solanke in the 43rd minute, who was dropped from the starting line-up following the Palace win.

De Zerbi's attacking options have already been ravaged by injury this season and the club will now be left to sweat over the extent of Tel's setback.

De Zerbi said: "Tel has a bad injury on his ankle, but I don't know how long [he will be out] yet."

Savio and Mykhailo Mudryk are out until after the international break, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are continuing to work their way back from serious knee injuries, with both eyeing returns after the turn of the year.

Tel has impressed for Spurs in recent weeks, scoring a stunning solo goal in their 2-0 win over Chelsea on 24 October, the club's first victory at Stamford Bridge since 2018.

articles.title: All Blacks down Scotland 43-21 and stay perfect in Nations Championship rugby
articles.summary: EDINBURGH, Scotland (AP) — New Zealand stayed undefeated against Scotland and perfect in Nations Championship rugby after taking an entertaining contest 43-2...
articles.body:
EDINBURGH, Scotland (AP) — New Zealand stayed undefeated against Scotland and perfect in Nations Championship rugby after taking an entertaining contest 43-21 on Saturday.

The All Blacks edged a seven-try shootout in the first half then shut out Scotland in the second half to take the tension out of Murrayfield for the last half hour.

The Scots rued near-misses against New Zealand in their three previous matches in 2017, 2022 and 2025 but could have no regrets this time as they succumbed to the weight of making a ton of tackles in the first half and the All Blacks' brilliant execution from set-pieces in the second spell.

New Zealand improved to 4-0 in the race with unbeaten South Africa to represent the southern hemisphere in the Nov. 29 final.

Scotland's own hopes were dealt a blow as it dropped to 2-2 in the northern standings with Australia coming next.

The All Blacks overcame two yellow cards to squeak out a 24-21 halftime lead as both sides turned down comfortable penalty kicks to go for tries.

articles.title: Notre Dame football fan, leprechaun nail $1.5 million ‘College GameDay’ kicks
articles.summary: The Notre Dame Fighting Irish could have a good omen heading into their battle with No. 1 ranked Miami on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Pat McAfee 's "Kicking is Easy" contest has taken a turn in recent weeks on " College GameDay. " The ESPN personality was giving out a lot of money early during the 2026 college football season, especially after SEC stops at Ole Miss and Texas.

In total, McAfee's given away over $14 million since the inception of his popular kicking competition.

Last week, an Indiana Hoosiers fan dramatically missed two consecutive kicks for the chance at $1 million. Saturday's trip to Notre Dame football included a special guest before the field goal contest even took place.

NFL and Fighting Irish great Joe Montana appeared on set to help give pre-med student Michael Milano some good luck. The lefty college football fan missed his first attempt wide right, but he made good on his second try despite McAfee making the contest even more challenging.

McAfee added to the show's theatrics by bringing out fake blockers, one of which featuring legendary Miami Hurricanes star Michael Irvin's face on it. Milano told Kirk Herbstreit and McAfee that he had never kicked before, but showed up to the event wearing cleats.

The Notre Dame student sent the Irish crowd into a frenzy after another successful kick in McAfee's contest.

Meanwhile, Milano's kick wasn't the only spectacle on Saturday morning. The Notre Dame leprechaun mascot named Riley also attempted a $500,000 kick that went to charity.

Montana and the Fighting Irish crowd watched the leprechaun drill his second kick after narrowly missing short on the first one. It could be a great omen for Notre Dame before the team's massive showdown with No. 1 ranked Miami on Saturday evening.

Notre Dame hosts Miami in a massive battle of AP Top 25 ranked teams. Kickoff from Notre Dame Stadium will begin at at 7:30 p.m. ET, and the game can be watched on NBC and Peacock.

articles.title: Here's how Gaylord, St. Mary and JoBurg volleyball fared in districts
articles.summary: The Gaylord-area volleyball season came to a close this week. See how Gaylord, St. Mary and JoBurg fared in their respective districts.
articles.body:
MANCELONA — Johannesburg-Lewiston's 2026 volleyball season has had a split theme: things they can control, and things they can't.

JoBurg (31-6-9) has done great with what they have been given; an injury to star player Mady Peppin to begin the year nearly spelled doom for the Cardinals, but multiple players stepped up in her place to help put up more than 30 wins and compete for the Ski Valley Conference title.

A number of things were outside the control of the Cardinals and head coach Kristine Peppin, however, including that devastating injury and, more recently, their district draw.

A healthy Peppin might have helped the Cards put together a run in one of the toughest Division 3 brackets but, with heavy hitters like Elk Rapids and Traverse City St. Francis awaiting them in the later rounds, it was going to take an all-out effort to make it through without her. After a 3-1 victory (25-21, 25-23, 11-25, 25-22) over Maple City Glen Lake in the first round, Elk Rapids defeated the Cardinals 3-1 (21-25, 18-25, 25-21, 18-25) in the semifinals, bringing JL's season to a close.

The Lily Crane-Emery Lawes duo continued to dominate the offense in the final two matches of the season, combining for 22 kills in the win over Glen Lake and 26 kills in the loss to Elk Rapids. Junior Hailey Bober finished a breakout season with two great performances, leading the team with 23 digs and four aces in round one and 28 digs and an ace in the semifinals.

It signals the end of the volleyball careers for seniors Mady Peppin, Lily Crane, Neela Lawes, Ashlynn Burke and Addison Lake, a group that helped JoBurg win a district title in 2025 and finish with over 30 wins in back-to-back seasons.

Key returners for next year's team include Emery Lawes, GraceLynn Lawes and Hailey Bober.

GSM battles to five sets vs. Boyne Falls, Gaylord swept by Petoskey

Gaylord St. Mary (6-23-1) had a chance to rewrite the headlines of its season heading into a Division 4 district bracket on Monday, Nov. 2, but came up just short in the semifinals vs. Boyne Falls (25-18, 19-25, 25-20, 23-25, 10-15) on Wednesday, Nov. 4, falling in the fifth set to bring the Snowbirds' 2026 season to a close.

Sophomore Laney Perdue was the top offensive threat all season for the Snowbirds, and her performance helped GSM jump out to a 2-1 lead after the first three sets. GSM nearly ended things in the fourth set, needing just two points to finish off a 3-1 upset victory, but Boyne Falls senior Olivia Pineda-Anderson fought through an ankle injury to lead her team to a comeback victory in set four, then helped the Loggers lead start-to-finish in a 15-10 fifth-set victory.

While their record might not show it, the Snowbirds' 2026 season had plenty of moments for coach Christie Perdue to be excited about the future, including the dominant three-set sweep of Wolverine (25-9, 25-10, 25-17) in the first round of the playoffs. GSM graduates one senior, Lily Keister, returning much of its core for 2027.

Meanwhile, the Gaylord Blue Devils (3-26-1) ended their season after a 3-0 sweep at the hands of Petoskey (19-25, 18-25, 14-25) on Monday, Nov. 2, ending a season that was seemingly doomed by injuries from before volleyball even started.

Sophomore Myla Montgomery was likely bound for a breakout season before a knee injury took her out of the lineup before the first match. By the time the season concluded, three more Blue Devils (Bindi Samalik, Jenna Wangler, Hadley Sorenson) joined her on the bench with various injuries, forcing lineup changes even up to the final week of the regular season.

Seniors Sarah Klepadlo, Maiya McDonald, Lily Willbee, Lily Lauer and Brooklyn Robertson say goodbye after helping guide the GHS program through a tumultuous era that included three different coaches in their final three seasons. Still, the youth coming up in the program should have the Blue Devils in a more stable spot in years to come.

articles.title: What does the Washington Nationals extension of Jacob Young mean for Dylan Crews?
articles.summary: With the extension of Jacob Young, what does the future of Dylan Crews look like and is he on the trade block?
articles.body:
Yesterday the Nats made a big move by extending Jacob Young. Paul Toboni inked the Nats center fielder to a 4-year $23 million deal with an option for a 5th year. We broke down the deal itself yesterday, but now I want to look at the bigger picture. Specifically, I want to examine what this means for Dylan Crews.

With the Young deal, the Nats now have James Wood, Daylen Lile, Dylan Crews and Young under team control into the 2030's. On the one hand, that is a great group of outfielders to have around for years to come. However, it also creates a surplus that you can trade from.

We know that Paul Toboni is not afraid to trade from a surplus. The most prominent example of that was the Curtis Mead trade, where he dealt a bat for an arm in Connelly Early. With Young locked up, the Nats now have a chance to make a similar sort of deal again.

Entering this offseason, I looked at either Dylan Crews or Jacob Young as potential trade pieces. They both profile as athletic, defense first right handed outfielders who are better against left handed pitching. Crews' pedigree, raw power and bat speed give him a higher offensive ceiling. However, Young is the better defender and had an OPS 45 points higher last season. Now that Young has been extended, a trade is likely to be off the table.

After this extension, I would bet executives have been calling Paul Toboni and asking about Dylan Crews. Obviously Crews has not lived up to his potential so far as a pro, but there are still traits to dream on for other teams. His bat speed, hard hit rate, barrel rate and average exit velocity are all above the 60th percentile. Crews also provided positive value as a defender and baserunner.

There would be plenty of teams that would be willing to take a shot on the 24 year old former top prospect. A Blue Jays fan account, who I think puts out very smart content, talked about how he either wanted Crews or Jacob Young. It makes sense for them, and plenty of other teams also need outfield help.

Now that Young is off the board, Crews would be the one to trade. However, a move is far from a given. We saw last season that there is enough playing time for both of them to get at least semi-regular at bats. The Nats used a DH rotation last year, which often allowed them to have Wood, Crews, Lile and Young in the lineup at the same time. There is no reason they cannot do this again.

The Young extension is also not total proof that the regime is out on Crews. At $5.75 million per year, the Nats are not exactly paying Young like a set in stone everyday starter. He will get plenty of playing time, but this extension does not automatically mean he will play every day.

It does mean that Young is in the team's long term plans though. If the right offer comes for Crews, I have no doubt that Toboni would pull the trigger. A Crews trade is certainly something worth monitoring. However, I do not necessarily think he is being shopped.

As for Crews himself, his 2026 season was very frustrating. It was not all bad, but there was just never enough consistency. Whenever he did something good, he was unable to take that momentum and run with it. The best example of this came after he got the Nats first walkoff hit in August. I thought this had a chance to be a real turning point for him, but instead he went 0 for 11 in the three games afterwards.

That pretty much summarizes his Nats tenure so far. However, he is entering his age 25 season and has shown flashes of excellence. If you do trade him, you run the risk of seeing him realize his potential with another team. On the other hand, it could also be the last time he has any real value. After the Young extension, this is a really interesting decision Paul Toboni has to make.

You see the talent when you watch Dylan Crews, but in 225 big league games, Crews has a .217 average and .648 OPS. That is simply not good enough for the former second overall pick. As we enter the offseason, the Nats have a decision to make. Do they give Crews another chance or is Paul Toboni happy to roll out an outfield of Lile, Young and Wood while getting the assets he can for Crews?

With the lockout less than a month away, we could get answers to that question pretty soon. There are cases for both sides, but I would certainly be listening to Crews trade offers now. I do not think there is any urgency to trade him, but after this Young extension, teams will definitely be calling about Crews. What would you guys do with the former LSU star?

articles.title: LeBron James laments his poor shooting night that snapped his 396-game streak
articles.summary: LeBron James had one of the worst shooting nights of his career on Friday night, and he knows the reason behind it.
articles.body:
After a strong start to the 2026-27 season, the Philadelphia 76ers have finally lost their second game. It was a 119-95 blowout loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers , which is an eye-opener for the 76ers after all their success.

It was a much-needed win for the Cavaliers , as they were floundering with a .500 record. Considering they had LeBron James coming back home for the game, it was a special night. However, it became a bad one for James because his streak of games in Cleveland with double-digit points ended at 396.

LeBron James did not like how poor the 76ers' shooting was against the Cavs

For the longest time, James had a hot streak with his regular season scoring. Despite struggling in some games, he still managed to score 10 or more points in the past 396 games he has played in the city of Cleveland.

Of course, James holds the record for that achievement because before he had this 396-game streak, he had a whopping 1,297-game streak of double-digit games from January 2007 to December 2025.

James had a quiet game against his hometown team, as he only had eight points, seven rebounds, and three assists. He only made three out of his 12 shots, one of the worst shooting nights of his career. However, it was not just him who had a rough night.

"Every game has its own challenges. Offensively, as a group, our offense was not good at all, and I know I damn sure wasn't good at all. I'm looking at the film and trying to get better from there," James said after the 76ers' loss to the Cavaliers .

It will be interesting to see how the 76ers bounce back from this. They have not faced much adversity this season, but with James as their leader, it will likely not be too much of a problem for them.

articles.title: New Zealand cruise to victory as Scotland fade
articles.summary: New Zealand canter to a 43-21 Nations Championship win at Murrayfield as Scotland fall away after a thrilling first half.
articles.body:
Tries: Sititi, De Groot, Taylor, Barrett 2, Moorby, Aumua Cons: McKenzie 4

Ruthless New Zealand blew Scotland away in a high-class, seven tries to three Nations Championship victory at Murrayfield.

Despite a historic first-half hat-trick from Scotland hooker Ewan Ashman, the All Blacks were mostly magnificent, unrelenting and classy. It was the 34th Test between the nations and New Zealand's tally has yet another win - 32 now, with two draws going back to 1905.

Wallace Sititi scored early in a breathless first half. Ashman responded. Ethan de Groot and Codie Taylor hit back to make it 17-7 at the end of the first quarter.

New Zealand's Peter Lakai was binned and Ashman got his second while he was off. The sensational Beauden Barrett scored the first of his double straight after. Then, as the bonkerdom stretched on, Sititi was yellow-carded and Ashman made the All Blacks pay with his hat-trick try.

Only three points divided them at the break, but the All Blacks outclassed Scotland thereafter. Josh Moorby, Beauden Barrett again and Asafo Aumua struck in the second half. Scotland were beaten out the gate in the end.

We hoped for a classic and a classic it was, with bells on. If only for 40 minutes. Beyond that thrilling opening spell it was one-way traffic, a vicious exhibition of All Black class and might.

Just like last year, when New Zealand drew first blood, the visitors came roaring out, punishing a penalty given away cheaply with a piece of trickery at a close-range line-out that bamboozled the Scots. A couple of dummy runners broke away and took enough of Scotland's attention with them. Sititi thundered through a gap to score.

Thus began the ding-dong. Kyle Rowe's magnificent 50-22 gave Scotland the field position to strike off a driven line-out - Ashman driving over for the first of his three tries. Unlike his counterpart, Damian McKenzie, Finn Russell converted. Scotland led by two.

New Zealand turned the screw again, forcing Scotland into big defensive set after big defensive set. There's only so much of that you can soak up, though. The visitors looked lethal from all corners. Beauden Barrett's surge downfield, hotly pursued by Matt Fagerson, was the catalyst for their second score.

Fagerson was done on the floor, New Zealand went to touch and De Groot went over the line. McKenzie converted; New Zealand by five. And, soon, New Zealand by 10. Another Scotland penalty was punished to the max, the All Blacks executing from the resultant line-out maul. Taylor getting it down this time.

This all happened inside the first quarter. On it went. Lakai, the terrific openside, was binned for persistent New Zealand offsides. Huw Jones almost scored but got held up. Scotland came again. Off a penalty advantage, Ashman blasted through Sititi to score. Two for the hooker. With Russell's conversion it was a three-point game.

Scotland needed to kick on, but instead they got pushed back. The wondrous Beauden Barrett sliced through following huge work from his pack; on the face it simple, but in reality, complex and beautiful. McKenzie restored the 10-point lead, but it didn't last long.

Sititi was binned for going off his feet. Scotland had a crack at 13 All Blacks for a brief minute but couldn't break them despite going painfully close through Jones. Lakai returned to make it 15 versus 14 - and that's when Scotland struck.

It was that old reliable again, the line-out maul proving devastating. Ashman got on the end of it and over he went for his hat-trick. For a flurry of penalties and back-to-back yellows, New Zealand got what they deserved. Those cards cost them 14 points.

Seven first-half tries and three points between them at the break. Now it was time for Test match animals to emerge. When they did, they were wearing New Zealand white rather than Scotland blue.

The All Blacks played those key minutes in Scotland's 22, forcing errors and penalties and opportunities. Off a scrum, Jordie Barrett's skip pass found Moorby in space and he sauntered over. Ruthlessness again. McKenzie converted; 29-21. And worrying.

More New Zealand heat and more Scotland penalties. Then, a yellow for Sione Tuipulotu. It could have been Ben White just as easily. The pressure the visitors were applying was just suffocating.

With the captain off the pitch, New Zealand made it pay - Quinn Tupaea to McKenzie and on to Beauden Barrett for his second of the day. Skill-set through the roof.

McKenzie's conversion made it 36-21. At 50 minutes, the game was over far too early for Gregor Townsend's side. To rub salt in the wound Aumua finished a gorgeous set-piece to land try number seven; 43-21 and 19-0 in the second half.

Scotland had hopes of winning or, at the very least, of taking New Zealand to the wire. The uneasy truth for Townsend and his players is that despite their excellence in the opening half, they were utterly bossed in the second.

These All Blacks are far more formidable than the version that appeared at Murrayfield a year ago. Meanwhile, Scotland's long, long wait for glory against the Kiwis carries on and on.

Scotland: Kyle Rowe; Kyle Steyn, Huw Jones, Sione Tuipulotu (capt), Jamie Dobie; Finn Russell, Ben White; Rory Sutherland, Ewan Ashman, Zander Fagerson, Gregor Brown, Scott Cummings, Matt Fagerson, Rory Darge, Jack Dempsey.

Replacements: Gregor Hiddleston, Pierre Schoeman, Will Hurd, Max Williamson, Josh Baylish, George Horne, Tom Jordan, Blair Kinghorn.
